:::{#thm-pois-deviance-residual}
#### Deviance residuals in Poisson regression

In a Poisson regression model,
the deviance residual of observation $i$ is

$$
d_i = \signt(y_i - \ey_i)
\sqrt{2\sb{y_i \logf{\frac{y_i}{\ey_i}} - (y_i - \ey_i)}}
$$ {#eq-pois-deviance-residual}

where $y_i \logf{y_i / \ey_i}$ is taken to be $0$ when $y_i = 0$.

:::

::: proof
The [saturated model](Linear-models-overview.qmd#def-saturated-model) fits each observation's mean exactly,
so its fitted mean for observation $i$ is $y_i$,
while the fitted Poisson regression model has fitted mean $\ey_i$.
A Poisson observation with mean $\mu$ contributes the log-likelihood term

$$
\ba
\llik(\mu; y_i)
&= \logf{\frac{\mu^{y_i} \expf{-\mu}}{y_i!}}
&& \text{(log of the Poisson PMF)} \\
&= y_i \logf{\mu} - \mu - \logf{y_i!}
&& \text{(log of a product and quotient)}
\ea
$$

For $y_i > 0$, the difference between the saturated and fitted terms is

$$
\ba
\llik_{\text{full}}(y_i) - \llik(\evb; y_i)
&= \sb{y_i \logf{y_i} - y_i - \logf{y_i!}} \\
&\phantom{={}} - \sb{y_i \logf{\ey_i} - \ey_i - \logf{y_i!}}
&& \text{(substitute } \mu = y_i \text{ and } \mu = \ey_i \text{)} \\
&= y_i \logf{y_i} - y_i - y_i \logf{\ey_i} + \ey_i
&& \text{(cancel } \logf{y_i!} \text{)} \\
&= y_i \paren{\logf{y_i} - \logf{\ey_i}} - (y_i - \ey_i)
&& \text{(group terms)} \\
&= y_i \logf{\frac{y_i}{\ey_i}} - (y_i - \ey_i)
&& \text{(quotient rule for logarithms)}
\ea
$$

For $y_i = 0$, the saturated mean is $0$,
and a Poisson variable with mean $0$ equals $0$ with probability $1$,
so $\llik_{\text{full}}(0) = \logf{1} = 0$, and

$$
\ba
\llik_{\text{full}}(0) - \llik(\evb; 0)
&= 0 - \paren{0 \cdot \logf{\ey_i} - \ey_i - \logf{0!}}
&& \text{(substitute } y_i = 0 \text{)} \\
&= \ey_i
&& \text{(} \logf{0!} = \logf{1} = 0 \text{)} \\
&= 0 - (0 - \ey_i)
&& \text{(the bracket in the residual formula, with } y_i \logf{y_i/\ey_i} \eqdef 0 \text{)}
\ea
$$

Substituting either case into the deviance residual definition
$d_i \eqdef \signt(y_i - \ey_i) \sqrt{2\sb{\llik_{\text{full}}(y_i) - \llik(\evb; y_i)}}$
gives @eq-pois-deviance-residual.
:::
